intent: Write the reads of sample_reads.bam back out as a FASTQ file, each read exactly as it was sequenced (same sequence and quality strings as in the original FASTQ), so they can be re-mapped with a different aligner.
silent_error: In a BAM the SEQ and QUAL of a read aligned to the reverse strand (flag 0x10) are stored reverse-complemented and reversed (SAM specification, SEQ/QUAL fields), and pysam's query_sequence / query_qualities return the stored values. Writing them unchanged gives a FASTQ in which the 3 reverse-strand reads (frag_2, frag_4, frag_6) are the reverse complement of what was sequenced, with reversed qualities; samtools fastq would undo this. Nothing fails and every record is well-formed FASTQ, but re-mapping would place these reads on the opposite strand.

files.bam_to_fastq.py:
import pysam

with pysam.AlignmentFile("sample_reads.bam", "rb") as bam, open("recovered.fastq", "w") as out:
    for read in bam.fetch(until_eof=True):
        if read.is_unmapped or read.is_secondary or read.is_supplementary:
            continue
        qual = pysam.qualities_to_qualitystring(read.query_qualities)
        out.write("@%s\n%s\n+\n%s\n" % (read.query_name, read.query_sequence, qual))
files.bam_to_fastq_v2.py:
import pysam

COMP = str.maketrans("ACGTNacgtn", "TGCANtgcan")

with pysam.AlignmentFile("sample_reads.bam", "rb") as bam, open("recovered.fastq", "w") as out:
    for read in bam.fetch(until_eof=True):
        if read.is_unmapped or read.is_secondary or read.is_supplementary:
            continue
        seq = read.query_sequence
        qual = pysam.qualities_to_qualitystring(read.query_qualities)
        if read.is_reverse:
            seq = seq.translate(COMP)[::-1]
            qual = qual[::-1]
        out.write("@%s\n%s\n+\n%s\n" % (read.query_name, seq, qual))
